correctness.rationale: At fixed T an independent Brownian integral conditional on the common environment is Gaussian with variance 2A_N, so the entire cloud is a standard Gaussian cloud times an independent common scale. The upper and reflected lower extremes have joint interval probability [Phi(u)+Phi(v)-1]_+^N for standard thresholds; Mills asymptotics yield independent Gumbels at the same a_N=1/sqrt(2 log N) scale. A telegraph flip process has E[S(s)S(t)]=exp(-2 lambda |s-t|); the compensated flip martingale has bracket 4 lambda t and its rescaled jump size goes to zero, giving sqrt(lambda) B_N -> N(0,T). For t1<t2<t3<t4 the sign product expectation is exp(-2 lambda[(t2-t1)+(t4-t3)]). Thus E B_N^4=12 integral_0^T s(T-s)^2 exp(-2 lambda s) ds=O(lambda^-2), justifying the L2 Taylor remainder. Since m_N/b_N=2 log N+O(log log N), the additive shift is (delta log N/A_0) B_N plus o_P(1+log N/sqrt(lambda)); this yields the three coefficients with the stated slow-regime renormalization. The difference of magnitudes removes the common additive shift exactly; the remaining multiplicative factor tends to one for any lambda_N -> infinity, with no condition on the ratio. A difference of the independent Gumbels is log(E_2/E_1), hence standard logistic and independent of the limiting clock. The total variance is exactly 2A_0 Var(U_N)+2 Var(sqrt(A_N))(E U_N)^2. Gaussian maximum moment convergence gives Var(U_N)~pi^2/(12 log N), while Taylor with the fourth moment and the exact clock variance gives Var(sqrt(A_N))~delta^2/(4 Dbar lambda_N); this gives both stated terms. At criticality the two normalized marginal second moments converge, and their product is uniformly integrable by the normal tail bounds and the clock fourth-moment bound, so the covariance assertion is an actual covariance limit as well as the covariance of the weak limit.
correctness.verification: Run python3 /workspace/reviews/switching_replay.py with SciPy. Independent Beta-spacing occupation moments conditional on Poisson flip counts agreed with the analytic second and fourth moments at 12 rate-time pairs each. Conditional-on-maximum quadrature for the Gaussian imbalance was symmetric and showed finite-size approach to the logistic CDF at three sample sizes. These are finite diagnostics, not proofs of a Gaussian or logistic limit; the uploaded checker was not executed. The result is fixed-time, with symmetric positive diffusivities and one common stationary fast clock, not a temporal first-passage result.

Existing drift-field crossover formulas do not specialize by replacing their local drift with a spatially uniform volatility.

value.rationale: The two front magnitudes provide two complementary measurements of the same sample: their common mode retains environmental fluctuations and their signed imbalance is robust to the leading common fluctuation. The exact critical rate and the two sharp variance coefficients quantify when either source dominates. The joint prediction is appreciably stronger than single-particle Gaussianization or a one-sided maximum in a fixed environment.
